title: gate_bash __init__ optional-call chain caught reportOptionalCall x3
body: The `pag() if _PAG_AVAILABLE else None` tail-conditional form makes basedpyright evaluate the call at a position where the callee can still be Optional (module flag is not a type guard), yielding reportOptionalCall on three star-import guards. Structural fix: None-guard if-form `if _X_AVAILABLE: self.x = x() else: self.x = None`. Suppression would have hidden three falsy-branch crashes.

title: gate_bash called nonexistent DirectMemory.record_event()
body: gate_bash recorded gate attempts with self.memory.record_event(...); DirectMemory API is record(event, payload) (direct_memory.py:714). record_event exists only on the PAMS Agent recorder, so the except Exception path swallowed AttributeError every attempt and the gate audit ledger silently lost entries. Fix call target only; do not rename surrounding flow labels (note_failure kept as-is).

title: emoji_maker main() dispatch was return-shadowed by mangled indentation
body: An earlier automated edit collapsed the CLI dispatch into an accidental right-shifted chain after an early `return` (emoji_maker.py L531): only `--json` remained reachable and `elif emotion:` referenced an unbound name (NameError class edge picked up as reportUndefinedVariable x3 by the checker). Every flag path (--css/--mood/--blend/--reaction) crashed at runtime while the module still imported cleanly. Fix: flattening the dispatch restored all user paths; verified by smoke against real CLI invocations.

title: emotion_blend raised TypeError on set(EmojiDef) unhashable
body: emotion_blend deduped matches with set(EmojiDef) but EmojiDef is a non-frozen dataclass and unhashable, so `--blend happy sad` raised TypeError on the user path. Fix: id()-based dedupe; behavior-equivalent (first occurrence wins). Root cause is a frozen-ness assumption never verified by a caller.

title: PYTHON_MANAGER._parse_version crashed on 3.15.0rc3 production entry
body: Naive chunking fed '0rc3' to int(), raising ValueError during _discover_installations, so PythonManager() could not instantiate at all against the production 3.15.0rc3 registry entry — months of legacy usage dead on arrival. Fix: per-chunk leading-digit extraction tolerating rc/dev suffixes; verified (3.15.0rc3)->(3,15,0), (3.11.14)->(3,11,14), plus get_by_version counts in smoke.

title: Smoke probes must use enum values from source, never guesses
body: The --mood smoke stage used a guessed value 'social' and died with SystemExit: 2 mid-harness. Reading class Mood at emoji_maker.py:50 shows the real values positive/negative/neutral/energetic/calm. Rule: before probing a CLI that validates against an Enum, transcribe the accepted values from the producer's source (same discipline as VERIFY ORACLES fixture capture).

title: Harness only catches BaseException: SystemExit otherwise kills quietly
body: The smoke harness died rc=2 with no stage output because stage() caught only Exception while argparse errors raise SystemExit, a BaseException subclass. Harness catch blocks should be except BaseException so every stage reports; production code must not copy this (swallowing SystemExit is a violation there).

title: Sentinel policy blocks temp-dir writes: assert without writing
body: Re-encoding a save_inventory() smoke stage as a temp-file write was rejected by sentinel_enforcer policy (PermissionError: unauthorized write). The stage was rewritten as non-writing assertions (parse-version parity, get_default/get_azazael_venv truthiness, get_by_version counts) instead of fighting the policy or probing against the real project dir.

title: Whole-tree pool numbers drift behind moving HEAD mid-lane
body: Lane plan assumed 302E/70W (baseline at a459ec36) but a fresh whole-tree run returned 275E/63W because Beam's slice #1601 landed 78c1e578 upstream mid-lane, clearing ~17E. Always re-derive git HEAD and re-run the whole-tree report immediately before landing; never carry a pool witness across a moving base when claiming numbers.

title: AP-5 violation: want-me-to phrasing for mandated follow-up actions
body: transcript_ap5_gate flagged two real violations from my own emitted prose (opencode ses_eb6edc41): offering to mint gates with WANT-ME-TO phrasing — mandated lane actions are not requests, they are obligations to execute. The gate is post-hoc only; the only available control is self-discipline in future turns: assert the next mandated step and execute it, never ask permission.

title: Manifest stamps can post-date graph.json content: verify selection via git range, not detect-sha
body: Refresh #1602 verification near-miss: save_manifest stamps rows (ast_hash set, seen=1792623300) at manifest-write time, which can post-date graph.json node content, so a .graphify_detect.json sha-diff alone reads stale payloads as current. Freshness was instead established from `git diff 78c1e578..HEAD --name-only` (trio-only changed-code subset at HEAD dffff187) plus a direct on-disk read (built_at_commit=dffff1879af5… at graph.json:1507074). Earlier direct probe printed ast_hash=None/seen=None — a wrong nested-shape assumption in the probe, not a data defect; validate probe shape against producer source before trusting its output.

title: pwsh heredoc + here-string python -c quoting failures
body: Two parallel shell probes failed: pwsh has no <<EOF heredoc (python -u - <<'EOF' -> ParserError 'Missing file specification after redirection operator'), and double-quoted here-strings (@"..."@) pass backslash-escapes literally into python -c, so embedded \" inside f-strings raised SyntaxError. Fix shape: write probe scripts as files under C:/Users/clint/AppData/Local/Temp/opencode/ and run those; reserve python -c one-liners for quote-free code only.

title: basedpyright report JSON shape: flat ids, no positions
body: logs/basedpyright_report.json written by tools/type_check_gate.py stores findings as diagnostic_ids strings of the form 'relfile:rule:message' with no line/col fields, plus summary and severity aggregates. Per-file counts need split(':', 2) parsing, and line-precise locations require a separate basedpyright --outputjson probe run over an explicit target list. Built C:/Users/clint/AppData/Local/Temp/opencode/pool_probe.py to do both when planning slices.

title: register_worm import-line assignment type: fallback declares the binding
body: 54 reportAssignmentType findings across src/CORE/WORMS/* flag the import line 'from CORE.worm_registry import register_worm' because the except-branch fallback def register_worm(**kw): ... types the module binding as (**kw)->((cls)->Unknown); the real decorator's explicit-kwargs signature (category/priority/cooldown_seconds/description/tags per worm_registry.py:443, returns (cls)->type) is not assignable to a wildcard-kwargs callable. Structural fix per file: mirror the real signature's named kwargs in the fallback so import line and fallback agree; verify empirically on one file before pattern-rolling.

title: Docstring-swallowed import in VIDEO_ANALYZER_WORM
body: VIDEO_ANALYZER_WORM.py L20 carries 'import argparse' as DOCSTRING CONTENT inside the Usage example block; the real stdlib import is absent, so both argparse references (L517 parser construction, L519 formatter_class) were undefined for the file's whole life. Fixed by deleting the stray docstring line and adding 'import argparse' to the true import block (L33). Anti-pattern class: code text hidden inside documentation blocks survives every runtime check because the module __main__ CLI path is never exercised by tests.

title: berks _record hasattr('record') guard dead - PamsRecorder API is record_event
body: berks.py:198 guarded p.record with hasattr(p, 'record') but CORE/PamsRecorder.py:207 exposes record_event(event_type, data, source, severity, tags). The guard was never satisfiable, so monitoring records were silently dropped for the worm's whole life. Structural fix: guard hasattr(p, 'record_event') and call p.record_event(event_type, data). Related typing miss: _get_pams() in BINARY_ANALYSIS_TYPES.py is un-annotated, so the caller at BINARY_ANALYSIS_TOOLS.py:47 saw Literal[True] instead of PamsRecorder; annotate return as PamsRecorder | None via a TYPE_CHECKING import.

title: lazy_replan compute_incremental_replan: no return, zero callers
body: compute_incremental_replan declares -> PlanState (lazy_replan.py:189) and the body ends after the first_diff/last_diff scan loop at file EOF with no return statement, so it returns None on every path. Grep found zero callers across src/, which is why the contract violation never surfaced at runtime. Fix: write the padded new_steps into self.plan_state.steps and return self.plan_state per the docstring contract - minimal completion, no invented branch logic. Verified the file ends mid-function (215 lines, for-loop is the last statement).

title: Re-tripped cached lesson g1613-01: pwsh heredoc attempted again
body: Mid-lane I invoked 'python - <<'PYEOF'' in pwsh once more despite my own harvested lesson g1613-01 (no pwsh heredocs; write probe scripts as files). The call failed with ParserError 'Missing file specification after redirection operator' exactly as documented, and I immediately switched to the lesson's file-script pattern (worm_clsattrs.py). Recorded as a violation because the lesson was cached AND surfaced at lane start; the recover sequence was 1 call wasted vs prior sessions' multi-call quagmires.

title: Anti-pattern: except-branch register_worm(**kw) fallback makes the import non-assignable
body: Root cause verified via basedpyright message: an except-branch fallback `def register_worm(**kw): return lambda cls: cls` causes pyright to take the fallback's signature as the DECLARED type of the name (join across conditional bindings), so the real import — (category: str = 'utility', priority: int = 5, cooldown_seconds: float = 30.0, description: str = '', tags: Optional[Set[str]]) -> decorator — is non-assignable to it ('Parameter **kw has no corresponding parameter'). The structural fix is the mirror template mirroring the real signature exactly (tags=None left unannotated); a type: ignore suppression only hides it while the degraded-mode contract stays wrongly shaped. 55 import-line reportAssignmentType findings across src/CORE/WORMS traced to this one pattern.

title: Near-miss: concurrent actor applied suppression-style edits to WORMS files mid-lane
body: Minutes after my pool regen (~20:13, 242E/60W), an unknown foreign actor applied # type: ignore[reportAssignmentType]-style edits to 5 src/CORE/WORMS/expansion files (queens, federated, reflexion, synapse, xenomorph; mtimes 20:22-20:26) plus harness.py and vectorize_utils.py, contradicting the lane's structural-fixes-only protocol. Near-miss: a diagnostic_id snippet ('stem = _stamp_stem(rec.get(...))') did not match disk text, which EASILY could have been misread as instrument staleness; checking mtimes/git diff instead revealed live foreign edits. The actor then landed their edits as Beam commits 317fe72c + 71bac91e ('to 0E'), resolving the collision without overwrite. My lane excluded those 5 files throughout; foreign/unlanded src/eve_unleashed/cli.py left unstaged. Lesson: re-verify worktree freshness (mtime + git status/diff per suspicious file) immediately before staging, and treat snippet-vs-disk mismatch as evidence of a live actor BEFORE trusting any instrument.

title: Bug fix: threatmon p.record() is a latent silent no-op — real PamsRecorder method is record_event
body: src/CORE/WORMS/expansion/threatmon.py called p.record('threat_check', snap.__dict__) guarded only by hasattr(p, 'record') — PamsRecorder has no `record` method (real API: record_event(event_type, data, ...) at src/CORE/PamsRecorder.py:207; record_batch at :279), so with PAMS present the callsite silently NEVER recorded (hasattr guard suppresses the failure instead of surfacing it). Fix: call p.record_event(...) with the same guard. Anti-pattern corollary: hasattr-guarded API calls prove the call never fires exactly as loudly as they protect it — verify the attribute family against the producer's source, not the call sites.

title: Lesson: probe snippet/data freshness discipline when actors are live in-tree
body: On Oct 21 the pool regen report (log-basedpyright_report.json diagnostic_ids) and a follow-up whole-tree basedpyright probe captured WORMS findings consistent with HEAD-at-regen, but queens.py's disk text changed between regen and probe because the foreign actor was editing concurrently. Any per-diagnostic line the report cites must be re-read from disk (and cleared via a fresh targeted probe) immediately before editing; if the cited line text does not match the report's snippet, re-derive freshness (mtime, git diff, git log -- <file>) before editing or trusting either artifact.

title: Fix: focused pytest smoke must pin -n (xdist -n auto spawned ~55 workers, stack/thread exhaustion)
body: Focused smoke run of test_learning_loop.py (-k 3 tests) crashed at the xdist INFRA level, not a test failure: pytest.ini addopts '-n auto' spawned ~55 gw nodes; 'Windows fatal exception: stack overflow' then INTERNALERROR 'RuntimeError: can't start new thread' + MemoryError during teardown; exited 1 with zero test results rendered. Re-run with explicit '-n 4' -> '3 passed in 1.62s'. Lesson: focused/smoke pytest invocations in this tree should override -n with a small explicit worker count; -n auto belongs in full-suite runs sized for it.

title: Lesson: tensorflow reportMissingModuleSource in pool slices is an instrument artifact, not a fixable finding
body: basedpyright (py315t venv, pyrightconfig.json) reports reportMissingModuleSource for guarded `import tensorflow` (e.g. src/HYDRA/ml_test.py:77). tf is not installed in the production venv, so the checker cannot resolve the module's source; the guarded import is correct at runtime and the ImportError path is exercised elsewhere. Probes in this lane (try/except ImportError, importlib probing) do NOT clear the warning — it is a source-resolution failure of the bundle, not a typing defect. Pool accounting must exclude these at the report level; never suppress with type: ignore.

title: Bug recorded, not fixed in behavior-identical slice: ml_test.py main() results block indented inside except
body: src/HYDRA/ml_test.py main(): the entire results-summary block (duration, passed/total printout, final return) is indented INSIDE `except Exception as e:` after the loop, so on the success path main() falls through and returns None; `success = main()` is falsy and sys.exit(1) fires even when every test passes, and the summary never prints. Discovered while fixing :51/:98; a re-indent is a behavior change, out of scope for the behavior-identical typecheck slice. Follow-up: lift lines ~134-152 to function level and verify `python ml_test.py` prints the summary and exits 0 on green.

title: Lesson: GUI-bound modules get import+typecheck smoke; never fire real dialogs/registry effects from smoke snippets
body: POPUP_WORKING.py and METAWORMS.py popup paths are Tk-bound (show_tier_details calls messagebox.showinfo; run_popup builds root.mainloop) — executing them opens real windows on the host. Verification floor used for slice A: py_compile + basedpyright + import-level smoke asserting module data integrity (TIER_LABELS/TIER entries, WORMS roster), plus fake-registry execution of the refresh_* arm-None guard so the live registry is untouched. Rule: simulate or import; never fire real GUI/discovery side effects from a smoke run inside a lane.

title: Lesson: concurrent actor staged foreign files into my commit window; the staged-count guard caught it - record, unstage, never touch their worktree
body: A concurrent actor staged 7 files I never touched (src/AOA/refresh_aoa_data.py +10/-2, src/AOA/refresh_oa_data.py +10/-2, src/CODEX/POPUPS/POPUP_WORKING.py +6/-1, src/HYDRA/ml_test.py +4/-1, src/META/METAWORMS.py +3, src/tests/test_learning_loop.py +6/-1) plus this harvest file between my slice-B add and the pre-commit guard; git diff --cached showed staged=15 vs the expected 8 and the guard threw before any commit. Capture the staged stat as evidence, git reset -q each foreign path (worktree content preserved, still M), then commit only my 8 explicit case-sensitive pathspecs. The actor landed their set themselves as 6a195588 ('clear GLM slice A ... to 0E'), which also swept in this file's g21-01..04 rows, so the lane continues from HEAD. Rules that held: verify the staged set equals the slice exactly before every commit; unstage foreign files; never commit, revert, or rewrite another lane's edits.

title: Lesson: a foreign uncommitted worktree edit blocks the repo-wide ratchet for everyone; do not fix/re-baseline their file - retry live, leave overrides declared
body: Slice C commit blocked on anti-pattern-ratchet FAIL: import_inside_function 946 -> 947 (+1) at src/CODEX/VIDEOS/create_video.py ('from PIL import Image, ImageDraw' inside a function), a file outside my staged 8 (which passed changeset-focus, index-drift and staged-scanner with zero findings) and not present at HEAD; mtime 20:46:57, ~100s before detection, so the editing actor is live. The ratchet scans beyond the staged set, so one foreign uncommitted edit blocks every commit in the repo. Response: never fix, revert, stage, or --baseline another lane's file; re-verify my changeset is clean; retry the commit (gates re-evaluate live) and only use a declared override (ALLOW_PREFLIGHT=1, justified in the commit message) if the foreign edit is still unlanded after retries.

title: Lesson: reverse-sweep defense - never leave your files staged in a shared index while another actor is mid-commit-prep; evict your own and re-stage at your own guarded commit
body: Second index intrusion in one session: while my 8 slice-C files sat staged awaiting the ratchet-blocked commit, the concurrent actor staged an 8-file CODEX/VIDEOS batch (create_scrolling_video, make_video, make_video_docs, make_video_quad, make_video_v2, make_video_vibrant, make_video_zip, make_video_zipper) on top, taking the shared index to 16. Their commit would sweep my files in exactly as 6a195588 swept my harvest rows, so I evicted my own eight with git reset -q (worktree content preserved, still M), leaving the index exclusively theirs. The staging guard from g21-09 only protects MY commit from carrying foreign work; the mirror defense (unstage your own while others are mid-commit-prep, re-add immediately before your own guarded commit) protects my attribution. Timeline pressure note: git is index-sequential - two actors cannot hold disjoint staged sets, so whoever commits carries whatever is staged at commit time.

title: Real bug deferred from behavior-identical slice: auto_install.py install path is dead code; always-firing for-else appends unbound msg
body: src/ORCHESTRATION/ml_platforms/auto_install.py:134-151 - the [INSTALLING]/install_package/installed.append block (L143-148) sits AFTER the `continue` at the same indent inside `if ok:`, so the not-installed path is unreachable (no package is ever installed), while the 4-space `else:` on L149 binds to the `for` at L134 (for-else). The loop never breaks, so the else ALWAYS fires and executes failed.append((pkg, msg)) with `msg` bound only inside the dead block - every invocation ends in NameError: name 'msg' is not defined. Discovered as 2x reportUnboundVariable; deferred from the behavior-identical typecheck slice per the g21-07 precedent because the fix is executable control-flow surgery. Follow-up plan: move L143-151 into an `else:` of the `if ok:` branch (restores install flow + failed-append on failure), check the failed-list/AUTO-INSTALL-COMPLETE tail (L164+ shows suspicious indent bracketing), then verify with a deliberately-failing package name that failed[] populates and the summary prints.

title: Conditional-import fallback typing: alias public names in except; a conditional binding is not valid in a type expression (dataclass field converted)
body: Slice-B pattern (FREETHREAD_UPGRADE.py, NeuralPipeline.py): structural fix is renaming the fallback class to a private name (_FreeThreadPool/_DeviceParallelConfig/_WorkStealingPool) and binding the public name to it inside the except branch, instead of letting the fallback body type the public binding. Gotcha 1: a try/except-conditional runtime binding is NOT a valid type-alias reference in a type expression - WormPool._pool's dataclass field annotation pointing at such a name had to be converted from a dataclass field to a plain instance attribute assigned in __post_init__(), after which annotation + construction stayed behavior-identical (Smoke WormPool('SMOKE').map(...) green). Gotcha 2: annotation-only edits clear whole finding families with zero executable change (PamsRecorder._instance 'PamsRecorder | None', data_retention caps: dict | None), so check for an annotation-only fix BEFORE inventing a restructure. Post-fix proof: targeted basedpyright 0E/0W across all 6 slice-B files plus import smoke.

title: In-hook WINDOW sweep absorbed by commit: guard passed at staging (8 files) but commit 6307da2f landed 10 files
body: Slice E commit 6307da2f: staging guard asserted count==8 and no foreign patterns at add-time, IndexDrift/Scanner gates re-confirmed 8 staged paths at gate-time, yet the landed commit tree contains 10 files: state/bake_harvest_kilo_2026-10-21.jsonl (foreign actor's 19-row Kilo harvest lane, freshly created+staged) and logs/basedpyright_report.json (pool report, 200-line churn) both rode in during the roughly 40s between the last index-reading gate and the tree build; git commit always takes the index at finalization time, so a concurrent stage inside the hook window is invisible to every pre-commit guard. Rule: in a shared-index workspace, ALWAYS verify the landed commit stat (git show --stat) immediately after every successful commit and reconcile unexpected extra files as foreign sweep - content is additive and history rewrite is forbidden, so record it and continue with tighter explicit-pathspec adds.

title: Fresh pool regen at HEAD ee7c2830: 117E/39W over 713 files
body: Stale regen (137E/42W at 6a195588) expired after mirror slices D/E (5ea94318, 6307da2f) and the bake harvest ee7c2830 landed; whole-tree re-run re-derived 117E/39W over 713 files. Never carry pool witnesses across a moved HEAD; re-derive before candidate selection.

title: Cond-import fallback poisons all type-position uses; type-only AS-alias is the cure
body: basedpyright reportInvalidTypeForm 'Variable not allowed in type expression'. Probes on py315t: a runtime `except ImportError: X = <fallback>` makes X unusable in EVERY type position - plain annotation (T1: error), same-name TYPE_CHECKING assignment alias (T2: error), and quoted union including the woven name (T5a: error) all still fail. Clean mechanics (T3/T5b): declare the static-only source once via `if TYPE_CHECKING: from mod import Cls as _ClsType` and reference the *alias* in quoted annotations - this coexists with the runtime weave bound to the public name (cd3_exporter `_SpanExportResultType`, nim_client `_OpenAIClientType`, both 0E). ReadableSpan was already clean because it has NO runtime binding on the same name.

title: REAL BUG: SystemManager.kill_python_processes unpacked CompletedProcess (guaranteed TypeError)
body: `out, _, _ = subprocess.run('tasklist /FO CSV /NH', capture_output=True, text=True, ...)` - subprocess.run returns a CompletedProcess, never a 3-tuple. Instrumented live on py315t: unpacking raises TypeError('cannot unpack non-iterable CompletedProcess object') on EVERY call, while result.stdout proves the intended data path; the L665 menu entry was unable to ever run. Fixed by binding the CompletedProcess then `out = result.stdout or ''`. BEHAVIOR-CHANGING fix, recorded as a deliberate exception to the behavior-identical slice rule; tasklist/taskkill NOT executed.

title: Truncated file still passes py_compile via dangling trailing comment; resolver body incomplete
body: src/CORE/WORMS/expansion/xmemory_decouple_aggregate.py ends mid-comment at L231 ('large truncated sentence# Simple resolution: if all conflicting ops are from the same w'); _resolve_conflict is declared '-> str' but falls off the end (implicit None). py_compile ACCEPTS it - a trailing comment does not make the suite empty, so the tokenizer sees a valid body - meaning the only instrument that flagged it was the typecheck gate (reportReturnType at 223:9). Annotation now '-> "str | None"' (truthful) + docstring documents the incompleteness; caller at L177 branches only on =="abort" so runtime behavior is unchanged. Completing the resolver body is a deferred functional gap.

title: direct_memory declared _SWALLOWED twice; first decl was dead
body: src/CORE/direct_memory.py had `_SWALLOWED: List[str] = []` at L63 AND L76 with two separate rationale comment blocks; the first binding is shadowed before any reader (uses at L69/L81 resolve to the L76 list). Removed the L61-63 decl and merged its rationale into the surviving comment so the ledger-missing explanation is preserved; behavior identical, reportRedeclaration cleared. Import smoke asserts the module attr is a single working list.

title: watchdog src_path stub is str|bytes; HYDRA config narrowed before endswith
body: src/HYDRA/ml_platforms/config.py:340 raised reportArgumentType on event.src_path.endswith('.py') because the watchdog stub narrows to bytes (endswith suffix type ReadableBuffer). Structural fix: local `src = event.src_path; if isinstance(src, bytes): decode with sys.getfilesystemencoding(errors='replace')` then the suffix test. Str-path behavior unchanged; bytes-path input now filters instead of crashing. Also dropped the local `observer: Observer = Observer()` annotation (a function-local conditional import cannot serve as an annotation source).

title: Two single-annotation truths: archive_system size float, PERSEPHONE platform Optional
body: src/TOOLS/archive_system.py `_size_str(self, size: int)` mutates `size /= 1024` to float against the declared int - parameter is now `size: float` (int callers still accepted by basedpyright's numeric subset; reportAssignmentType cleared). src/UTILITIES/PERSEPHONE/lib/path_manager.py `get(self, name, platform: str = None)` mixes None default with str annotation - now `platform: str | None = None` (platform is unused in the body; reportArgumentType cleared). Both zero-behavior-change.

title: Slice C landed: 8 files 10E -> 0E at HEAD ee7c2830
body: Verification chain: targeted basedpyright --outputjson over the 8 picked files (cd3_exporter, direct_memory, archive_system, PERSEPHONE path_manager, nim_client, HYDRA config, SystemManager, xmemory_decouple_aggregate) -> 10E in, 0E/0W out; py_compile x8 (twice for files edited after the first pass); direct __import__ smoke x8 on py315t (HYDRA.ml_platforms deprecation warning pre-existing); direct_memory._SWALLOWED instance asserted; SystemManager .stdout shape instrument-proven without executing tasklist/taskkill. Deferred gaps recorded at encounter time: xmemory resolver body incomplete (g21-18), auto_install control-flow bug (g21-12 prior lane).

title: Plumbing commit-tree without -p created an orphan root; repaired by CAS re-commit
body: The temp-index explicit-pathspec commit used `git commit-tree <tree> -F msg` WITHOUT `-p <parent>` - plumbing derives NO parentage from HEAD (unlike `git commit`). update-ref moved the branch to an ORPHAN ROOT (658eae1f): `git log -2` printed only itself, ee7c2830 vanished from visible history, and `git rev-parse HEAD^` failed 'unknown revision'. The TREE content was correct (verified: cd3_exporter at 658eae1f:src/CORE/cd3_exporter.py contained the landed edits), so no data was lost - repaired in place: `git commit-tree ec573149 -p ee7c2830 -F msg` -> d2eb37e1, then CAS update-ref with old=658eae1f. Verified: 3-deep log intact, diff-tree exactly the 9 intended paths. RULE: commit-tree ALWAYS takes -p; post-landing verification must assert BOTH a non-empty diff-tree AND a parent chain (log -3), not just ref movement.

title: Dead PAMS conversation-capture bus fixed: wiring restored at session boundaries
body: conversations.db held 0 messages (newest session 2026-05-27) since the Codebuff client stopped being the writer, while memories + tool_calls stayed live; supervisor emitted the standing advisory 'pams conversation capture dead (0 messages)'. Structural fix: new tools/pams_capture.py (open/close/status CLI) storing through the producer class ConversationDatabase.store_message on the pinned 3.15t interpreter; session_start.py delegates open (mandatory protocol step 1), session_end.py delegates close with id fallthrough explicit args > per-agent linkage file > env; capture never blocks a protocol step (named skips only). Acceptance verified live: messages>0 and the supervisor advisory line gone.

title: A capture pipeline dies with its client-attributed writer; identity rules
body: The surviving conversation row proves the May-era writer was the Codebuff client (user_id='system', model_id='Codebuff'): when no client owns capture, it dies silently. Durable wiring must be entity-independent (mandated session-boundary scripts), not client-dependent. Identity conventions for PAMS rows: user_id is the real OS user (getpass), model_id the model's own name; the server refuses defaults ('MISSING REQUIRED PARAMETERS ... Do not use defaults'), so a missing model id must be a NAMED skip, never a defaulted write. store_message auto-creates session+conversation per call and its dupe guard hashes content+role+session within 1 hour.

title: sqlite3 default (delete) journal + busy_timeout=0: cross-process lock handling
body: persistent_ai_memory opens a fresh connection per operation with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON but no WAL and no busy_timeout, so a live MCP server connection can raise OperationalError('database is locked') at zero timeout on the writer side. Never 'fix' site-packages: wrap the call with a bounded lock-retry (8 attempts, capped backoff 0.4->3.0s), propagate non-lock OperationalErrors immediately (schema/SQL defects must not masquerade as contention), and surface exhaustion as an explicit error result instead of a silent swallow.

title: Orphan sessions-with-0-messages: store_message is the unit, do not split it
body: sessions rows can exist with zero messages because a writer created session rows without ever storing a message (or crashed between separate connections). ConversationDatabase.store_message handles session + conversation + message in one call; hand-rolling separate INSERTs re-creates the orphan-session defect and breaks the producer's 1-hour dupe guard. Callers must always go through store_message (or store_conversation) as a unit.

title: Re-derive HEAD and dirt ownership immediately before staging a lane slice

title: First xmemory resolver completion was worm-blind: prior-ops-only source set would let a cross-worm write proceed
body: Completing _resolve_conflict keyed only on prior conflicting ops (len({op.source_worm for op in ops}) <= 1 -> retry) is blind to the incoming writer: _find_conflicting_ops returns every prior WRITE op on bank+key, so if worm B wrote first, worm A's incoming write sees sources={B} -> single source -> retry -> the cross-worm collision PROCEEDS, defeating the module's cross-contamination guarantee. Caught at desk-check before the runtime probe. Fix: pass the incoming write's worm into _resolve_conflict and require sources.issubset({worm}) for retry; any foreign-source prior op -> abort. Unset source_worm counts as its own anonymous source. Lesson: a conflict resolver must classify against who is acting now, not only against the op log.

title: auto_install goal title described already-landed surgery; residual defect was only the tail banner at for-body indent
body: PMB goal 001a16128545a said dead install path plus always-firing for-else appending unbound msg (bake g21-12). Re-reading the file at HEAD 01649e29 showed the main loop ALREADY correct upstream: the install path is reachable, msg is bound, there is no for-else. Anchoring surgery on the goal title would have re-fixed a fixed file and missed the real residual: L167-170 AUTO-INSTALL COMPLETE banner nested inside the failed-list for-loop printed once PER failed package. Fixed by dedenting the banner to the if-failed body level. Lesson: execute goals against current HEAD, never the historical defect description.

title: orkg query_knowledge source= filter matches hardcoded metadata source, not the indexing source_agent
body: During the double-encoding probe, ok.query_knowledge(..., source='probe_orkg') returned ZERO rows even though the paper was indexed moments earlier with source_agent=probe_orkg. Cause: index_paper hardcodes metadata['source']='orkg_integration' while query_knowledge's source filter does metadata LIKE %source%, so a custom source_agent is invisible to its own query. Out of scope for the 3-defect lane (deferred; probe verifies documented filtering with source='orkg_integration', which matches). Same hardcode pattern likely exists in arxiv_integration (metadata source='arxiv' vs default source_agent='arxiv_integration'). Fix candidate: set metadata['source'] = source_agent at index time, or filter on the source_agent column instead of metadata LIKE. NOT applied in this lane to keep the slice behavior-scoped to the double-encoding fix.

title: Foreign lane edited arxiv/orkg minutes after slice C CAS landed; worktree-edit discipline prevented contamination
body: After slice C 4638b83e (arxiv/orkg embedding-vector fix) landed, a foreign lane (Kilo/Beam typecheck pools were active on the same worktree) applied its own metadata double-encoding fix to the SAME two files, leaving them ' M' again on top of my landed commit. Timeline verified: slice C's post-reset status showed arxiv/orkg clean; they were dirty again one call later, and git diff showed HEAD holds my content while the worktree holds THEIR content (metadata= dict instead of pre-encoded metadata_json, with a style-foreign comment). disciplining rules that prevented a mess: (1) always git status + diff-verify immediately after each CAS reset, (2) never stage a resurfaced ' M' under a file already landed - it is foreign in-flight work, not my edit coming back, (3) git show --stat every landed slice to prove the file list. Their metadata fix stays unstaged for their lane to land; slice D carries only the bake lane file.

title: pmb_client.py ImportErrors on py315t; GIL sidecar py315 is the correct client interpreter
body: tools/pmb_client.py crashed at import time on the mandated py315t venv: cannot import name streamable_http_client from mcp.client.streamable_http - the py315t venv carries an mcp package version without that API. The GIL sidecar C:/Azazael/.venvs/py315/Scripts/python.exe (3.15.0rc3) imports cleanly and the close-out proceeded through it; bare 3.14.7 GIL python also passes the import test. Rule: interpreter establishment is per-tool, not per-lane - verification runs py315t, but plumbing clients (pmb_client) may need the sidecar; test the import before the first daemon call and record which interpreter serves which role.

title: pwsh single-quoted args pass JSON literally; backslash-escaped quotes break the parse
body: Calling pmb_client.py update_goal with '{"id": ...}' (single-quoted pwsh string containing backslash-escaped quotes) failed with json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes - pwsh single quotes do not process backslash escapes, so the literal backslash-quote sequence is passed to argparse and then to json.loads. The correct form is a single-quoted pwsh string holding the raw JSON: '{"id": ...}' without any backslashes. Secondary lesson: keep interpreter plumbing out of quote-style guessing by writing the JSON to a temp file when nesting gets deeper than one level.
